spec.description: Black cubic and increasing line, arrowed axes and curve ends, no ticks or numerical labels. Both bounded regions are shaded with the house light green.

answer.worked:
The intersections satisfy
$$\begin{aligned}x(x-4)^2&=x\\x\big((x-4)^2-1\big)&=0\\x(x-3)(x-5)&=0\\x&=0,3,5.\end{aligned}$$
The cubic is above the line on $0<x<3$; the line is above the cubic on $3<x<5$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_0^3\big(x(x-4)^2-x\big)\,dx+\int_3^5\big(x-x(x-4)^2\big)\,dx\\&=\int_0^3(x^3-8x^2+15x)\,dx-\int_3^5(x^3-8x^2+15x)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{8x^3}{3}+\frac{15x^2}{2}\right]_0^3-\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{8x^3}{3}+\frac{15x^2}{2}\right]_3^5\\&=\left(\frac{63}{4}-0\right)-\left(\frac{125}{12}-\frac{63}{4}\right)\\&=\frac{63}{4}+\frac{16}{3}\\&=\frac{253}{12}\text{ units}^2.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
The curves share a tangent at $A$, so their gradients are equal there.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dx}(x^2)&=\frac{d}{dx}(\ln x+k)\\2x&=\frac1x\\x^2&=\frac12\\x&=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\quad(x>0\text{ since }\ln x\text{ is defined})\end{aligned}$$
Then $y=x^2=\frac12$, so $A=\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\frac12\right)$.

Since $A$ lies on $y=\ln x+k$:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac12&=\ln\frac{1}{\sqrt2}+k\\k&=\frac12+\frac12\ln2=\frac{1+\ln2}{2}\end{aligned}$$
The curve $y=\ln x+k$ meets the $x$-axis where $\ln x=-k$, so
$$b=e^{-k}=e^{-\frac12}\cdot2^{-\frac12}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2e}}.$$
Let $a=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$. The required region lies under $y=x^2$ for $0\le x\le a$, with the part under $y=\ln x+k$ for $b\le x\le a$ removed. Using the given primitive:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area}&=\int_0^{a}x^2\,dx-\int_b^{a}(\ln x+k)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{a}-\Big[x(\ln x-1)+kx\Big]_b^{a}\\&=\frac{a^3}{3}-\Big[x(\ln x+k-1)\Big]_b^{a}\end{aligned}$$
At $x=a$: $\ln a+k=\frac12$, so the bracket is $a\left(\frac12-1\right)=-\frac{a}{2}=-0.35355\ldots$

At $x=b$: $\ln b+k=0$, so the bracket is $b(0-1)=-b=-0.42888\ldots$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area}&=\frac{\sqrt2}{12}-\left(-\frac{\sqrt2}{4}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2e}}\right)\\&=\frac{\sqrt2}{3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2e}}\\&=0.11785\ldots-\left(-0.35355\ldots-(-0.42888\ldots)\right)\\&=0.04252\ldots\end{aligned}$$
The area is $0.04252$ square units, correct to four significant figures.

children.prompt: Find the points of intersection of the two curves shown, that is, the three points of intersection with the smallest positive $x$-coordinates.

answer.worked:
Since $f'(x)=1+\cos x\ge 0$, with $f'(x)=0$ only at isolated values of $x$, $f$ is strictly increasing.
Suppose $f(x)=f^{-1}(x)=y$. Then $f(x)=y$ and $f(y)=x$. If $x<y$ then $f(x)<f(y)$, so $y<x$, a contradiction; similarly $x>y$ is impossible. Hence $y=x$, so every intersection lies on $y=x$ and satisfies $f(x)=x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}(2x-1+2\sin x)&=x\\2x-1+2\sin x&=2x\\\sin x&=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$$
The three intersections shown have the three smallest positive solutions $x=\dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{13\pi}{6}$.
Since $y=x$ at each point, the points are $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6},\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$, $\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6},\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{13\pi}{6},\dfrac{13\pi}{6}\right)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the shaded area enclosed by the two curves.

answer.worked:
No formula for $f^{-1}$ is needed. The graphs of $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are reflections of each other in $y=x$, and both lobes are bounded by the two curves between consecutive intersections on $y=x$. The line $y=x$ therefore splits each lobe into two pieces that reflect into each other, so
$$A=2\times(\text{area between }y=f(x)\text{ and }y=x).$$
Now $f(x)-x=\sin x-\dfrac{1}{2}$. This is positive on $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6},\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)$ and negative on $\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6},\dfrac{13\pi}{6}\right)$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=2\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{5\pi}{6}}\left(\sin x-\frac{1}{2}\right)dx+2\int_{\frac{5\pi}{6}}^{\frac{13\pi}{6}}\left(\frac{1}{2}-\sin x\right)dx\\&=\Big[-2\cos x-x\Big]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{5\pi}{6}}+\Big[x+2\cos x\Big]_{\frac{5\pi}{6}}^{\frac{13\pi}{6}}\\&=\left(\sqrt{3}-\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)-\left(-\sqrt{3}-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+\left(\frac{13\pi}{6}+\sqrt{3}\right)-\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}-\sqrt{3}\right)\\&=\left(2\sqrt{3}-\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)+\left(2\sqrt{3}+\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\\&=4\sqrt{3}+\frac{2\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$$

In the required region,

= ∫₋₁² (x + 2 − x²) dx

= [x²/2 + 2x − x³/3]₋₁²
= 10/3 − (−7/6)
= 4.5 u²

Let f(x) = x²(1 − x) and g(x) = x(1 − x)²
f(x) − g(x) = x(1 − x)(x − (1 − x)) = x(1 − x)(2x − 1)

= 2(1/8 − 1/8 + 1/32)
